text:
customer-JKL: Hey @maria — we've been seeing a weird regression since yesterday's rollout. Our virtual assistant started giving different answers to the same prompt within a single conversation.

customer-JKL: Example: user asks for company refund policy, first reply was correct and quoted our policy. Immediately re-sent the same prompt (no context change) and got a short, incorrect summary that contradicts the policy. Happening across multiple users and endpoints. Request IDs below.

customer-JKL: request_id=req_9f3a2b, endpoint=/v1/chat, model=redwood-large-v1
customer-JKL: request_id=req_9f3a2c, endpoint=/v1/chat, model=redwood-large-v1-quant

customer-JKL: repro curl (sanitized):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-large-v1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"What is the refund policy for cancelled subscriptions?"}],"session_id":"sess-42"}'
```

maria: thanks for the examples — sorry about this. I'm escalating. Can you confirm whether the inconsistent outputs are all from the same session_id or different? Also, do you see any HTTP 5xx or 429s around those request_ids?

customer-JKL: All from the same session_id (sess-42). No 5xxs, occasional 429s earlier today but timestamps for these requests show 200 OK with differing text.

devin: I'm looking at routing logs now. Initial trace for req_9f3a2b: routed to host pool "hosted-nyc-1" -> backend instance rwd-serve-12 -> model_variant redwood-large-v1.
devin: For req_9f3a2c (same session, later in conversation): routed to host pool "hosted-nyc-2" -> backend instance rwd-serve-18 -> model_variant redwood-large-v1-compat (we call it the compat fallback).

devin: Log snippet: 
```
[2026-03-14T13:41:02Z] TRACE route_decision request=req_9f3a2b customer=JKL session=sess-42 target_model=redwood-large-v1 route=primary host=hosted-nyc-1 instance=rwd-serve-12
[2026-03-14T13:41:05Z] TRACE route_decision request=req_9f3a2c customer=JKL session=sess-42 target_model=redwood-large-v1 route=fallback host=hosted-nyc-2 instance=rwd-serve-18 variant=redwood-large-v1-compat
```

zoe: that align with a suspicion — our fallback routing intentionally picks a compatible variant if the originally requested variant isn't available on the selected pool. Problem is, the compat variant has a slightly different tokenizer/knobs and we didn't mark it as "session-sticky". So within the same session requests can hit different variants when routing chooses different pools.

andrew: yep — there's a known gap: session affinity is based on customer+session hashing to a pool only when that pool advertises sessionAffinity:true. If a pool is saturated, the router will pick a different pool and may use a compatible variant. We increased global autoscaling earlier which temporarily moved some traffic and our canary changed pool weights.

maria: immediate mitigation options — 1) pin JKL to exact model_variant for the rest of the session (quick), 2) rollback the canary routing weight change (broader), 3) add a server-side check to prefer session-sticky variant when session_id present (requires dev rollout). Thoughts?

customer-JKL: we need something fast — option 1 or 2 works. Pinning would be great.

devin: I can push a policy override for customer JKL to pin model_variant=redwood-large-v1 for the account's active sessions. Doing it now.

support-bot: Created ticket CS-4321: "Inconsistent model outputs within single session due to routing fallback". Assigned to dev team routing+ml, priority P1.

deploy-bot: Canary update 2.3.5 routing-adjust published at 2026-03-14T08:12:00Z -> affected pool weights: hosted-nyc-2 +8%

devin: override applied for customer JKL: policy_pin{customer=JKL, model_variant=redwood-large-v1, ttl=4h}. Confirming subsequent requests are routed consistently to redwood-large-v1.

customer-JKL: after your pin, I re-tested the earlier prompt twice in the same session — both responses match and are correct. Thanks.

zoe: root cause summary: routing fallback to compatible variant + lack of session affinity enforcement across pools. The compat variant has a slightly different generation configuration leading to output divergence for edge prompts (policy/legal language).

andrew: long-term fix items:
- guarantee session affinity at router level: hash(customer+session) -> prefer same model_variant across pools when possible (spec + tests)
- annotate model_variant metadata with a "compatibility_delta" flag so we can block auto-fallback for customers with strict semantics (like TOS/policy)
- add regression alert that monitors "semantic drift" within a session (diffs between first and subsequent replies above threshold)

maria: immediate actions I will take: 1) keep pin in place for 24h, 2) open RFC for session-affinity changes and compat flag, 3) notify infra to watch autoscaling/pool weights while canary runs.

devin: also adding unit+integration test to routing: simulate session requests, force pool change, assert that for session-sticky customers the variant does not change.

customer-JKL: appreciated. Do you have an ETA for final fix? We rely on consistent language for compliance.

maria: we'll triage the RFC today. Target for a code-change release in the next sprint (2 weeks) with hotfix options if needed sooner. I'll follow up in CS-4321 with timelines.

customer-JKL: ok, thanks. We're unblocked for now. Please keep us posted. :pray:

support-bot: CS-4321 updated: mitigation=pin applied, status=investigating, sla=24h.

maria: marking this thread resolved for customer contact; leaving the ticket open for engineering follow-up.

customer-JKL: verified stable across 30+ runs. Closing on our side — will re-open if we see any more drift. Thanks team! :tada:

zoe: noting for postmortem: add model variant semantics doc and a short how-to for support to apply short-term pins for critical customers.

maria: thanks everyone. Good catch, and good triage.
